eras.i: Lincoln. The monetary fight Bryan lost twice to McKinley. A central bank. The 1929 crash. A New Deal that briefly held the bust in place. A postwar order built around a dollar pegged to gold.
eras.ii: After the war, an intelligence apparatus designed for a global contest. Where elected governments became inconvenient, it removed them. Iran. Guatemala. Indonesia. Chile. The body count from this period runs into the millions. By 1975 the public read enough of the agencies' own files to ask what else.
eras.iii: The dollar comes off gold. Reagan rolls back the postwar policy stack. September 2001 reopens the playbook for foreign wars. The bailouts that follow run the opposite direction of the New Deal's.
eras.iv: Citizens United legalizes the money. Snowden documents the mass collection. The Epstein files surface and disappear. Gaza is funded, armed, and shielded. Palantir, OpenAI, and the data-center race come for the rest.
eras.v: Eras I through IV document the systems. Era V documents the people running them — named, on the record, with primary sources and witnesses.

anchors.y1981-israel-islamist-counterweight: After taking Gaza in 1967, Israel licensed and funded Sheikh Yassin's Islamist charity Mujama al-Islamiya as a counterweight to the secular PLO. The military governor told the New York Times in 1981 that the money came out of his budget. The charity was the seedbed Hamas grew from in 1987.
anchors.y2025-foreign-aid-terror: February 26, 2025. A House Oversight hearing on foreign aid. A Middle East Forum witness testified that U.S. money had reached the Taliban, Hamas, Hezbollah, al-Shabaab and others. That testimony sits against the U.S. aid watchdog's own account of where the money goes.
anchors.y2026-ct-strategy: May 6, 2026. The White House releases the United States Counterterrorism Strategy, the document a national-security presidential memorandum (NSPM-7) called for after the Kirk assassination. For the first time, a standing threat category covers domestic left-wing extremists, anarchists and anti-fascists, and the strategy pledges to map the memberships of groups whose ideology it calls anti-American.
anchors.y2026-ndaa-224: May 2026. The House Armed Services Committee marks up the FY2027 defense bill. Section 224 directs the Secretary of Defense to name an executive agent to synchronize U.S.-Israel weapons R&D and co-production across ten domains — among them artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and “network integration, data fusion.” The text comes from Ronny Jackson's U.S.-Israel FUTURES Act. On June 4 the committee rejected an amendment to strike the section by voice vote; two members supported it.
anchors.y1900-mckinley: 1900. The election that set U.S. monetary policy — gold standard, tariffs, overseas expansion — and the Oz allegory scholars later read into it; Trump has cited McKinley as a model since 2024. Nearby: Ingersoll Lockwood's 1890s “Baron Trump” novels and his “The Last President.”
anchors.y1913: The Federal Reserve Act creates a central banking system: a board of governors over regional reserve banks owned by member commercial banks, mixing public and private authority over the money supply. Commercial banks create money when they lend, but they do not create the interest owed back on it.
anchors.y1929-crash: 1929. The first full demonstration of how the system behaves when a leveraged expansion reverses: collapsing prices on one side, fixed-by-contract debts on the other, and a directional transfer of real assets to whoever still has cash.
anchors.y1933: The New Deal: a policy stack that pulled measured U.S. inequality to its lowest level for thirty years.
anchors.y1944: Forty-four allied nations meet at a New Hampshire resort and design the postwar monetary order around a U.S. dollar pegged to gold. The IMF and the World Bank are created here; the arrangement holds until Nixon ends gold convertibility in 1971. Alongside it: the federal seizure of Nikola Tesla's papers after his 1943 death, and the MIT engineer John G. Trump who reviewed them.
anchors.y1945-paperclip: 1945 onward. The U.S. military-intelligence program that brought more than 1,600 German scientists, including former Nazi Party and SS members, into U.S. government employment — among them the V-2 designer Wernher von Braun.
anchors.y1947: The National Security Act creates the CIA. Fifteen years later, the Joint Chiefs would formally propose remote-controlling civilian aircraft and “orchestrating terrorism in U.S. cities” as a pretext for invading Cuba. Kennedy rejected it. The declassified document is filed under this entry.
anchors.y1948-genocide-convention: 1948. The legal architecture for what counts as genocide is written. What it leaves out — political groups — is what makes most of Era II's killings unaddressable under it.
anchors.y1953: Wernher von Braun's Mars-mission novel, written in 1949 after Operation Paperclip brought him to the United States and published in English in 1953. In it, the elected head of the Martian government holds the title “Elon.”
anchors.y1953-mkultra: April 1953. CIA Director Allen Dulles authorizes Project MKULTRA, a mind-control research program that ran human experiments, often on unwitting subjects, with LSD, hypnosis, sensory deprivation, and electroshock. Most of its records were destroyed before it surfaced publicly.
anchors.y1954: Operation PBSUCCESS. The CIA-backed coup against Guatemala's elected president Jacobo Árbenz, and the thirty-six-year civil war that followed.
anchors.y1956-cointelpro: 1956 to 1971. The FBI's domestic surveillance and disruption program, targeting U.S. political organizations from the Communist Party USA to the Black Panthers, the SCLC, the women's movement, and the Klan. The November 1964 “suicide letter” the FBI mailed to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. — published in unredacted form in 2014 — is the canonical documentary artifact.
anchors.y1964-tonkin: August 1964. The Johnson administration cites a second North Vietnamese attack on U.S. destroyers in the Gulf of Tonkin to push the Tonkin Gulf Resolution through Congress and authorize military force in Southeast Asia. A 2005 NSA declassification confirmed that the second incident did not occur.
anchors.y1965: October 1965 through March 1966. The Indonesian anti-communist purge. The U.S. embassy's role and the CIA's own 1968 assessment of the killings — declassified — are filed under this entry.
anchors.y1965-vietnam: U.S. ground combat in Vietnam, 1965–1975, plus the spillover into Cambodia and Laos, neither of them U.S. enemies on paper.
anchors.y1972-watergate: The June 1972 break-in at the Democratic National Committee cost Nixon the presidency two years later. The records here cover the landslide, the target, the cover-up tape, who ran the operation, and the FBI deputy director who guided the reporting — and separate that documented record from the claim that intelligence agencies staged Watergate to remove a president who knew who killed JFK.
anchors.y1973: September 11, 1973. A U.S.-backed coup overthrows Chile's elected president Salvador Allende and installs Pinochet; the Church Committee later documented the covert support.
anchors.y1975: The Church Committee. A year of Senate hearings on the conduct of the CIA, FBI, NSA, and IRS — and the largest single declassification of intelligence-agency conduct in U.S. history.
anchors.y1975-condor: Operation Condor. The Southern Cone military regimes' coordinated cross-border campaign of state terror, run on infrastructure the United States helped supply.
anchors.y1971: Nixon closes the gold window. The Bretton Woods arrangement ends; the dollar becomes a fiat currency.
anchors.y1980: Reagan rewires the postwar economic compact. From this point on, the gains from rising productivity stop reaching the typical worker, whose pay had tracked it since the war.
anchors.y1980-el-salvador: El Salvador's civil war, 1980–1992: the U.N. Truth Commission's findings, and the U.S. role in training the death-squad battalions.
anchors.y1998-iraq-sanctions: 1998. Two senior U.N. coordinators resign, in succession, over the U.N. Security Council's sanctions regime on Iraq. Both publicly call it genocide.
anchors.y2001-attack: An event still being argued about. The records here cover verifiable threads from on and around the day — questions about timing, physical evidence, and who knew what when — each with its citation.
anchors.y2001-aftermath: A CIA officer goes on television in 2007 to confirm the agency tortured. He is prosecuted in 2013. The Senate publishes its own study in 2014 — 6,700 pages, of which 525 are made public.
anchors.y2002-netanyahu-iraq: September 12, 2002. Former Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu testifies before the U.S. House Committee on Government Reform on the case for invading Iraq. The premise on which he testified — that Saddam Hussein was on the verge of nuclear weapons — did not hold up in the aftermath.
anchors.y2003: The invasion of Iraq, justified by claims about weapons of mass destruction that did not exist. The intelligence apparatus that produced the case is the same one whose conduct the Senate documented in 2014. Direct and indirect casualty estimates from the war run into the hundreds of thousands.
anchors.y2003-emf-patent: A U.S. patent from the early 2000s describes manipulating a person's nervous system by pulsing images on a nearby monitor or TV. The card sets the granted patent — its issuing agency, its private inventor, its blank assignee field, and its 2021 expiry — against the framing that treats a patent as proof the method works or was ever deployed.
anchors.y2008: The global financial crisis. A first Government Accountability Office (GAO) audit of the Federal Reserve's emergency lending, the recovery's distributional outcomes, and the foreclosure totals.
anchors.y2010: Citizens United v. FEC. The Supreme Court rules that political spending is speech and that corporations have the same speech rights as people. One result: a single megadonor's nine-figure gift to a 2024 presidential campaign.
anchors.y2013: Edward Snowden hands the Guardian and the Washington Post a complete archive of NSA bulk-collection programs — PRISM, Boundless Informant, Stellar Wind — and flees the country. The leaked documents contradicted the legal arguments the NSA had made in secret. The infrastructure he documented is still in operation.
anchors.y2016-west-hospitalization: A concert cut short, a tour cancelled, a 911 call placed from his trainer's house. Six years later Kanye West posted a screenshot he said was that trainer threatening to have him institutionalized and medicated again, and the trainer's earlier career turned out to be a real one: research scientist at a Canadian Department of National Defence laboratory that tested wakefulness drugs on soldiers. What follows separates the documented sequence and the documented credentials from the inference stacked on top of them.
anchors.y2017-bennington: Four high-profile cultural figures — Chris Cornell (Soundgarden, May 2017), Chester Bennington (Linkin Park, July 2017), Avicii (Tim Bergling, April 2018), and Anthony Bourdain (CNN, June 2018) — die in fourteen months. Each death is individually ruled suicide. A claimed documentary tying them together — “The Silent Children” — does not appear in any verifiable production record, but the speculation it represents has circulated continuously since. What is documented is each death itself, and the FBI's own 2007 bulletin on the symbols pedophiles use to identify themselves.
anchors.y2019-zelensky: Volodymyr Zelensky played a president on television before he was elected to the office: a comedy series on a channel owned by the oligarch backing him, a party named after the show, a candidacy launched on that channel's New Year's Eve broadcast, a 73% win, and elections later suspended under martial law. The claim that U.S. intelligence engineered all of it leans on a 2013 State Department spending figure that predates his candidacy by six years.
anchors.y2019-cufi: Christians United for Israel, founded by John Hagee in 2006, claims more members than there are Jews in the United States. The IRS designates its parent entity a church, so it files no public financial reports. Israeli-government money reached it through a Ministry of Strategic Affairs cut-out, and it commands striking access in Washington — a sitting Vice President, Secretary of State, and National Security Advisor on one stage, with the Prime Minister of Israel on the satellite feed.
anchors.y2019: Jeffrey Epstein is arrested July 6, 2019. He is found dead in his Manhattan jail cell on August 10. The two guards assigned to his floor sign false log entries. The two cameras pointed at his cell malfunction. By the next year, Ghislaine Maxwell has been arrested and convicted; many of his named clients have not. The opening poll on this page records what the public thinks happened. Around the case: the DOJ Files Transparency Act records, the recurring “body count” and death-list claims weighed against the documentary record, and the documented convictions of several media figures.
anchors.y2020-pandemic-response: March 2020. The COVID-19 financial-market disruption and the Fed's three-month response, then a split outcome: asset prices recovered while real wages eroded.
anchors.y2021-surfside: 1:22 a.m., June 24, 2021. The Champlain Towers South in Surfside, Florida partially collapses; 98 dead. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) traces the cause to the pool deck, the corroded reinforcing steel, and warnings on paper since 2018. In the same hours, separately, John McAfee dies in a Spanish prison cell. Both events are documented; the connection drawn between them online is examined here.
anchors.y2022-eskridge: Huntsville, Alabama. The death of plasma physicist and antigravity-research startup founder Amy Eskridge in 2022 — ruled a suicide, contested in some quarters as targeted suppression — and Trump's 2025 decision to relocate U.S. Space Command headquarters to Redstone Arsenal in the same city. The institutional history of Huntsville as the postwar landing site of the German rocket scientists relocated under Operation Paperclip is the backdrop both records sit against.
anchors.y2023: October 7, 2023 begins the latest phase of the conflict in Gaza. The Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research estimates more than 100,000 conflict-related deaths in Gaza by October 2025, with life expectancy falling to nearly half what it would have been without the war. The campaign is funded, armed, and diplomatically shielded by the United States. Three threads run through the chapter: the war and its toll, the U.S. funding and lobbying behind it, and Netanyahu's corruption trial at home.
anchors.y2023-food-supply: Three separately documented items, often presented as a single chain: WEF white papers promoting alternative proteins over livestock, the CDC's 2023 count of tick-borne alpha-gal meat allergy, and a Gates-funded effort to genetically engineer a cattle tick. Each card states what its primary sources establish, and where the record ends and inference begins.
anchors.y2023-antarctica-icecube: A former South Pole contractor says the IceCube neutrino detector is a directed-energy weapon that triggered the 2011 Christchurch earthquake. The card sets his account beside the facility his operators document and the cataloged cause of the quake.
anchors.y2023-palestine-laboratory: Systems tried out under occupation become an export line. A prize-winning book gave the pattern a name; the cluster runs from Elbit's border towers to a US-police training pipeline, an Israeli spy-van maker's corporate lineage, and the Caribbean operation where the exported gear now points at migrants.
anchors.y2014-stingray: A cell-site simulator impersonates a cell tower so nearby phones connect and reveal themselves. US police bought them in secret, under FBI nondisclosure agreements that kept the devices out of open court.
anchors.y2024-pagers: September 17–18, 2024. The Hezbollah pager-and-walkie-talkie operation: a supply-chain assassination at scale, devices rigged with explosives before delivery and detonated en masse.
anchors.y2024: Palantir's defense contracts compound; its Maven Smart System becomes the U.S. military's targeting backbone. Alongside it: the FBI's access to commercially purchased bulk data, raised at a 2026 Senate threats hearing.
anchors.y2025-kirk: Charlie Kirk is shot once in the neck at a university debate in Utah, in front of 3,000 people. Prosecutors identified and charged the accused shooter within 48 hours, citing DNA and cartridge-casing evidence; the federal ballistic comparison to the recovered rifle came back inconclusive. Alternative explanations have circulated, including the claim that an exploding lavalier microphone, not a bullet, caused the wound, and assertions that other people in the field of view were involved. Each is documented under this entry alongside what the official record states.
anchors.y2025: Where the page lands as of mid-2026. The threads above are presented together, with citations, so the reader can assess them.
anchors.y2026-pineal-system: A five-step 'control system' theory circulates online: chemtrail aluminum, vaccine aluminum, glyphosate as cotransporter, fluoride as pineal binder, and 2.45 GHz Wi-Fi as activator — framed as intentional environmental design producing a manageable population. Each step borrows vocabulary from real laboratory work: Luke 2001 on pineal fluoride deposition, Bigay 1987 on aluminofluoride G-protein activation in vitro, Mitkus 2011 (FDA) on vaccine aluminum pharmacokinetics, Mesnage 2017 on the Seneff/Samsel glyphosate commentaries, and Shearer 2016 on what 77 atmospheric chemists reported about secret aerial spraying. Each step rests on real chemistry; the coordinated-control synthesis does not appear in the literature.
anchors.y2021-anthropic: December 2020. The Anthropic founding split from OpenAI. The stated reason: a different model for how AI should be scaled, and how the people building it should be trusted.
anchors.y2023-altman-firing: November 17, 2023. The OpenAI board fires Sam Altman, citing a lack of consistent candor. He is reinstated five days later. Ronan Farrow returned to the board's reasoning two years later.
anchors.y2026-altman: April 2026. Ronan Farrow and Andrew Marantz publish a long New Yorker investigation alleging a pattern of deception by Sam Altman, drawn from internal memos and named, on-record sources — including a senior Microsoft executive.
anchors.y2026-ai-bubble: U.S. AI capital expenditure is running at roughly 5% of GDP; past infrastructure buildouts have busted economies at around 3%. Unlike railroads, highways, or fiber, the GPUs in this buildout obsolesce every three to four years. Daniel Priestley, who called the 2008 crash early, has forecast a reckoning around 2029.
anchors.y1917-balfour: November 2, 1917. The 67-word letter from British Foreign Secretary Arthur Balfour to Lord Walter Rothschild — issued during World War I, while Palestine was still Ottoman territory — committing the British Empire to facilitate a Jewish national home in Palestine. The competing British wartime promises to Arab independence and to France over the same territory are part of the same diplomatic record.
anchors.y1920-pre-state-militias: The institutional record between the first Rothschild-funded colonies and the founding of Israel. The armed organizations that guarded the early settlements ran in an unbroken line into the army of the new state, and several of their commanders became its prime ministers. What each group did, and what the British, the United Nations, and contemporaries called them at the time, is documented below.
anchors.y1948-mockingbird: From the late 1940s onward. The CIA's recruitment of U.S. journalists and editors as intelligence assets and propaganda conduits — surfaced through the 1975-76 Church Committee and Carl Bernstein's October 1977 Rolling Stone reporting.
anchors.y1948-nakba: 1948. The Palestinian “catastrophe.” Approximately 750,000 Palestinian Arabs displaced and 400 to 600 villages destroyed in the war that began with the U.N. partition vote and continued through the establishment of the State of Israel.
anchors.y1967-chaos-minaret: August 1967 onward. The CIA's Operation CHAOS and the NSA's Project MINARET — twin programs targeting the U.S. anti-war movement and civil-rights leaders for surveillance, exposed by Seymour Hersh in 1974 and the Church Committee in 1975.
anchors.y1967-six-day-war: June 5-10, 1967. Israel's preemptive strike against Egypt and the war that followed — at the end of which Israel held the West Bank, Gaza, East Jerusalem, the Sinai, and the Golan, roughly tripling the territory under its control.
anchors.y1985-iran-contra: 1985 to 1986. The Reagan administration's covert sale of weapons to Iran in exchange for the release of American hostages in Lebanon — and the diversion of the proceeds to the Contras in Nicaragua, in violation of an explicit Congressional ban. Independent Counsel Lawrence Walsh's 1993 report is the canonical record.
anchors.y1985-pollard: November 1985. The arrest of U.S. naval intelligence analyst Jonathan Pollard for selling classified material to Israel. Sentenced to life in prison, paroled after thirty years, parole expired November 2020, flown to Israel December 2020 aboard a Sheldon Adelson private jet.
anchors.y1990-gladio: October 1990. Italian Prime Minister Giulio Andreotti formally acknowledges Operation Gladio — the Italian arm of a NATO-coordinated network of clandestine paramilitary “stay-behind” cells across Cold War Western Europe, elements of which had been linked to right-wing terror operations during the Italian “Years of Lead.”
anchors.y1991-casolaro: August 10, 1991. Freelance investigative journalist Danny Casolaro is found dead at the Sheraton Hotel in Martinsburg, West Virginia, on the trip he had told his brother could end with his death. The notes for the book he called The Octopus — which traced Inslaw, BCCI, the October Surprise, and Iran-Contra as a single network — were missing from the room.
anchors.y1996-clean-break: July 1996. The Institute for Advanced Strategic and Political Studies presents incoming Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu with a strategy paper — “A Clean Break” — drafted by Richard Perle, Douglas Feith, David and Meyrav Wurmser, and others, recommending regime change in Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, and Iran. Several authors went on to senior Bush administration posts during the 2003 Iraq invasion.
anchors.y1997-dtca: August 1997. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration loosens disclosure requirements for direct-to-consumer broadcast advertising of prescription drugs. The United States and New Zealand remain the only two countries that permit such advertising aimed at consumers in mass media.
anchors.y2007-wesley-clark: March 2, 2007. Retired General Wesley Clark — former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe — tells Democracy Now! about a 2001 Pentagon memo describing a plan to remove the governments of seven countries in five years: Iraq, Syria, Lebanon, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, and Iran. The Iraq invasion in 2003, NATO Libya operation in 2011, Syrian civil-war involvement, and 2025 strikes on Iran have substantially intersected the list.
anchors.y2007-haarp-earthquake: A former Forbes Asia bureau chief says Japan's finance ministry was coerced under threat of an 'earthquake machine,' and names HAARP. The card sets his account beside the Alaska research facility on the documented record and the cataloged cause of the 2007 quake that hit the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa nuclear plant.
anchors.y2018-nation-state-law: July 19, 2018. The Knesset passes Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People. Between 2021 and 2022, B'Tselem, Human Rights Watch, and Amnesty International each independently conclude that Israeli policy in territory under its effective control meets the international legal definition of apartheid. With it: U.S. state anti-BDS statutes, and Israeli-ministry funding of U.S. campus advocacy disclosed under foreign-agent law.
anchors.y1865-lincoln: April 14, 1865: President Lincoln is assassinated at Ford's Theatre, five days after Appomattox. Around it, the war's money: the Confederacy's European cotton-bond loan and the cabinet officer who ran it, and a banker-conspiracy quote long misattributed to Lincoln.
anchors.y1913-frank-adl: 1913. Leo Frank — Cornell-educated factory superintendent and the sitting president of B'nai B'rith's Atlanta Gate City Lodge — is tried and convicted for the murder of thirteen-year-old Mary Phagan. In direct response to the case, B'nai B'rith founds the Anti-Defamation League in October. Frank is lynched in August 1915 after Governor Slaton commutes his death sentence to life in prison.
anchors.y1993-adl-spying: April 8, 1993. San Francisco police and the FBI raid the Anti-Defamation League's (ADL) San Francisco and Los Angeles offices, seizing a 400-page affidavit that alleges the ADL held confidential government information on more than 1,000 people — Arab Americans, the anti-apartheid movement, the NAACP, ACT-UP, Greenpeace. No criminal charges followed; a 1999 class-action settlement required a partial records purge.
anchors.y2012-mcafee-belize: April 30, 2012. Belize's Gang Suppression Unit raids John McAfee's compound in Orange Walk, killing his dog. McAfee says it was retaliation for refusing to pay a politician; he is detained, released without charge, and flees the country seven months later after a separate murder investigation names him a person of interest. His 2021 death in Spanish custody is covered in a later entry.
anchors.y1960-nmmp: 1960. The U.S. Navy acquires its first dolphin for hydrodynamic studies of torpedo design. By 1962 the program has become the Marine Mammal Program at Point Mugu; it has trained dolphins and sea lions for mine detection and harbor-protection missions in Vietnam, the Persian Gulf, and Iraq, and was declassified in the early 1990s.
anchors.y1888-wolf: April 1, 1888. Washington lawyer Simon Wolf — longtime president of the Jewish fraternal order B'nai B'rith, and a Lincoln-era confidant who later carried European Jewish-rights questions to several U.S. presidents — publishes a pamphlet, The Influence of the Jews on the Progress of the World, written as a direct answer to the antisemitic agitation of the 1880s. In plain affirmative language it states four claims that recur almost verbatim a century later in conspiratorial narratives about Jewish influence: the Rothschilds and the European money market, Jewish ownership of the European press, Jewish stimulus of European revolutionary politics, and — nine years before Herzl — America as Palestine and the rejection of a Jewish national restoration in Jerusalem.
anchors.y1895: 1895. With the Treasury's gold reserve nearly gone, the solvency of the United States was restored not by the government but by a private banking syndicate led by J.P. Morgan and the Rothschilds' American agent. It is the early American instance of the pattern the Federal Reserve chapter picks up next door: when the state needs money, it turns to the houses that already hold it, and the arrangement is made out of public view.
anchors.y1843-bnai-brith: October 13, 1843. Twelve recent German Jewish immigrants — led by Henry Jones (born Heinrich Jonas) and including Isaac Rosenbourg — meet at Aaron Sinsheimer's café on New York's Lower East Side and found Bundes-Brüder, soon better known by its Hebrew name Bnai Brith (Sons of the Covenant). The order takes its motto — Benevolence, Brotherly Love, and Harmony — and writes a constitution committing the lodge to the traditional functions of European Jewish societies: visiting the sick, protecting widows and orphans. From this nucleus the order becomes the largest Jewish fraternal-and-advocacy organization in the world, begins publishing The Menorah in 1886, supplies a generation of Jewish-American public figures including its longest-serving president Simon Wolf, and in 1913 founds the Anti-Defamation League in Chicago in response to the Leo Frank case.
anchors.y2026-dawg: April 29, 2026. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, testifying before the House Armed Services Committee on the Department of War's FY2027 posture, announces that the United States will shortly stand up a sub-unified command for autonomous warfare. The accompanying budget unveils a 4.6 billion line for the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group (DAWG) — a roughly 24,000-percent jump from the 25.9 million the same office received the year before, larger than the Marine Corps budget, and the headline of a 4 billion aggregate drone and counter-drone request the Pentagon calls the largest such investment in U.S. history. Alongside the testimony and budget line sits the Phantom MK-1 humanoid-robot program — Foundation Future Industries, a San Francisco startup whose chief strategy adviser is Eric Trump — already holding 4 million in Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase 3 Pentagon contracts, with two combat humanoids on the ground in Ukraine.
anchors.y1960-cuba-embargo: The economic blockade of Cuba, and the internal memo that set out its purpose before it began. It has outlasted ten U.S. presidents.
anchors.y1987-sankara: Burkina Faso's president argues to the assembled African heads of state that foreign debt is a means of control, and presses for a collective refusal to pay. He is killed in a coup the same year.
anchors.y2011-libya: The 2011 NATO intervention that ended Gaddafi's rule and fractured Libya. At issue is a contested account of the motive, drawn from a released State Department email.
anchors.y1963-dimona: Israel built a secret reactor in the Negev with French money and engineering. For two years Kennedy pushed to open it to American inspectors; the paper trail of that fight sits in the National Security Archive. The pressure lapsed after his death, and the United States has neither inspected nor acknowledged the arsenal since.
anchors.y2017-pentagon-trillions: When the Defense Department's own Inspector General cannot trace where money went, the entry is logged as an “unsupported adjustment” — a documentation failure, not a finding of theft. The figure that grew out of the 2001 Rumsfeld disclosure became the basis for both a forensic-accounting question and a much larger “stolen trillions” narrative.
anchors.y2026-follow-the-money: Four pieces, in sequence. In 2019, former central bankers working at BlackRock proposed that in the next downturn the Federal Reserve should put money into the economy directly. In 2020 the Fed expanded dramatically, and asset prices recovered faster than wages. In 2025 a federal law set rules for dollar-pegged stablecoins and required them to hold Treasuries as backing, so money moved into stablecoins also funds government debt. The same year, an executive order began opening 401(k) retirement accounts to crypto and private equity. In 2026 Peter Thiel, a PayPal and Palantir co-founder, moved his family to Argentina. Whether these form a single plan or a series of separate incentives is left to the reader.
anchors.y2025-mrna-cancer: Two 2025 observational studies reported a cancer association in COVID-vaccinated groups. Both report correlation, not causation: one signal reversed once a 12-month lag was imposed, and the same study found lower all-cause death among the vaccinated.
anchors.y2021-pfizer-papers: A Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) suit forced Pfizer's vaccine licensing file into public view, after the FDA proposed releasing it over decades and a federal judge ordered a far faster pace. The file holds a biodistribution study and a post-authorization adverse-event tally; contested reanalyses have been built on top of them.
anchors.y2021-moderna-recall: Foreign particles in Moderna vials triggered a lot suspension and a joint manufacturer investigation in Japan. The card below records what the particles were identified as, and the manufacturing cause investigators assigned to them.
anchors.y2021-graphene-oxide-claim: Where the graphene-oxide-in-vaccines claim comes from, and what the analysis behind it actually established. The card below carries the report it rests on, the caveats its own author placed on it, and the independent reviews that tested it.
anchors.y2017-emf-smart-meters: Radio-frequency energy from smart meters, and the chart of power-density 'harm thresholds' that circulates with it. The cards below trace where that chart's numbers come from and set out the exposure limits regulators actually enforce.
anchors.y2026-covid-origins: On May 13, 2026 a CIA officer who ran the intelligence community's COVID-origins review testified under subpoena that the lab-leak finding his analysts repeatedly reached was overridden from above, and that Fauci steered the inquiry toward a curated list of his own funded experts. The sworn allegations sit below next to the documents and the rebuttals — what the testimony states, and what is asserted on top of it, kept separate.
anchors.y2026-safety-signals: A Senate investigation put ~600 pages of internal FDA email into the record: an FDA data-mining expert showed her bosses, starting March 1 2021, that the system in use was hiding vaccine safety signals, and a better method surfaced about 25 of them. She was told to stop. What the emails say and where the senator's framing runs past them are kept apart below. Sits alongside the other COVID chapters on this timeline.
anchors.y1910-flexner: A 1910 survey of North American medical schools set the template for how doctors would be trained — research- and laboratory-based, drug-centered — and helped close the schools that taught otherwise, including all but two of the country's Black medical colleges. Who paid for the rebuild, and to what end, is where documented fact gives way to contested motive.
anchors.y1985-processed-food: Two decades after the government named cigarettes a cause of lung cancer, the companies that sold them bought the companies that feed the country. What followed: the brands, the flavor science, and the federal advice on what to eat.
anchors.y2021-chronic-disease: What Americans eat and what treating them costs, in the government's own numbers — the share of children's calories that now comes from industrially formulated food, and the share of national health spending that goes to chronic and mental-health conditions.
anchors.y2024-drug-money: The money inside the drug system: who pays to have new drugs reviewed, and what one family took out of the company that seeded the opioid crisis. The figures here are the audited and court-tested ones, which run lower than the rounder numbers in circulation.
anchors.y2025-residual-dna: Trace DNA left over from manufacturing is expected in these vaccines; the dispute is over how much, and over one gene-control sequence found inside the Pfizer product that was not on the filed ingredient list. Independent labs, a state-senate witness, and the FDA each read the same finding differently.
anchors.y2003-darpa: Two DARPA programs from the early 2000s aimed to pull a person's whole record — communications, finances, movements, contacts — into one searchable system. Congress cut off Total Information Awareness in 2003; LifeLog was canceled the next year, on the day Facebook launched. The cards separate what is documented — the programs, their goals, the dates, the CIA money that later seeded Palantir — from the argument that the surveillance simply moved to the private sector to escape oversight.
anchors.y2024-project-panama: February 2024. Anthropic hires the man who ran partnerships for Google Books and gives him a target: every book there is. The pipeline that follows buys used print copies, cuts them apart, scans them, and throws the paper away. The planning page has a codename and an instruction not to talk about it. A year later a federal judge holds that the destruction is the part that makes it legal.
anchors.y2026-fauci-hsgac: Subpoenaed to a Senate committee about the pandemic, Fauci answered nothing — not the substance, and not the day of the week. The senators' case is that a pardon takes the privilege away; the precedent they cite says that, and also says why a witness might still claim it. Below: what happened in the room, what the pardon covers, and what the released emails show about the award money.
anchors.y1961-sv40-polio: Polio vaccine was grown in monkey kidney cells, and the monkeys carried a virus nobody was testing for. Testing rules arrived in 1961; the lots already on the shelf stayed there. Whether the exposure caused cancer has never been closed out — the government's own review found the biology plausible and the population data unable to settle it.
anchors.y2021-early-treatment: Two repurposed drugs were argued to make the vaccines unnecessary. Both got large randomised trials, including in the early-outpatient window their proponents specified. The results are below, with the methodological objection that is still made against them.
anchors.y2021-vaccine-paperwork: Two documents nobody could read: a package insert that shipped blank, and 148 pages of CDC myocarditis correspondence released with every word blacked out. The reasons differ — one is how emergency authorisation distributed prescribing information, the other is a discretionary FOIA exemption applied to every line. Both are real, and neither means what it is usually said to mean.
anchors.y2025-visa-speech: A State Department speech set a visa standard against foreign nationals who "foment hatred against our Jewish community," and drew no line between that and criticism of the Israeli government. The transcript is public; the threshold is not.
anchors.y2026-shaping-the-record: Three mechanisms that decide what reaches a reader: an initiative to shape how chatbots describe Israel, the crowd-rated labels that replaced Meta's fact-checkers, and the bot accounts an Israeli broadcaster counted in its own politics.
anchors.y2026-haredi-draft: A 2024 court ruling ended the blanket exemption for yeshiva students. Two years on, most enlistment orders go unanswered, arrests are rare, and the Knesset's attempt to bar those arrests is frozen in court.
